target_customer: Nigerian and emerging-market employers and individuals who buy health insurance and care plans
problem: Quality healthcare in Nigeria is hard to access and afford. The company began as a telemedicine app and grew into an HMO with its own clinics.
business_model: Health insurance premiums (HMO) plus telemedicine and owned clinics

founders.name: Femi Kuti
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/CEO. Press says the company began as Kangpe, a telemedicine app.

founders.name: Matthew Mayaki
founders.role: Founder, Senior Vice President Product (bio says VP Engineering)
founders.background_notes: YC bio calls him a software engineer with over 5 years of experience.

technical_complexity.rationale: Telemedicine app plus claims and insurance operations. Difficulty is in regulated insurance operations and clinic building, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: HMO licensing, provider networks and employer contracts are hard to replicate quickly, though large HMOs such as Hygeia already existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought it in the sources found. Hygeia appears only as a profile comparison without date.

market_need_then: Nigeria had low insurance coverage and limited access to doctors. No dated 2017 data was opened, so need is inferred from the telemedicine origin and the later insurance pivot.

branding.domain_note: Uses getreliancehealth.com, a prefixed domain, per the YC page.

brand_strength.rationale: Recognized in Nigerian health and tech press after the large Series B, but the name is generic and shared with other Reliance companies, and no brand-focused source was found.

pivots.to: HMO with insurance, telemedicine and owned clinics
pivots.why: Not stated explicitly. A profile says Kangpe later added an insurance arm.

outcome_analysis: Reliance Health moved from a telemedicine app to an HMO with clinics, raised a $40M Series B led by General Atlantic in 2022, and expanded to Egypt in 2022. A single directory says it cut 106 jobs in July 2025 chasing breakeven, which suggests expansion economics were strained, but that is unverified.
notes: Seed of $2M in June 2017 comes from Digest Africa and is consistent with the sources' total of $48M ($40M plus $6M plus $2M) but is not confirmed by a second outlet. Series A in January 2020 and the $40M Series B are from search summaries of TechCrunch and General Atlantic; Partech participation in the Series B is inferred from a Partech press URL title and is not stated. A third co-founder, Opeyemi Olumekun, appears in one search summary without an opened source, so he is not listed. The 106-job cut in July 2025 and Egypt and Senegal underperformance appear on single aggregators and are unverified. Company site fetch was rate-limited. Founding year conflicts: 2015, 2016 and 2017 across sources.
